The '''Solaran Language''' is the vernacular language of [[Solara]]. It developed from the older ceremonial language [[Solra]], also called the Elder Tongue, and became the everyday language of Solaran homes, commerce, newspapers, schools, military orders, and public administration.

By the late nineteenth century, Solaran was central to national integration. The adoption of the [[Solaran Alphabet|Sunline]] writing system made mass literacy easier and helped connect provincial schools, newspapers, government offices, and commercial records to a single written standard.

== Relationship To Solra ==

Old source material sometimes uses '''Solra''' as an alternate name for the vernacular language. A separate source page, however, identifies [[Solra]] as the Elder Tongue: an older ceremonial, liturgical, and legal register associated with temples, state ritual, and elite education.

This draft separates the two terms for clarity. '''Solaran''' refers to the modern vernacular language, while '''Solra''' refers to the older prestige language from which Solaran developed.

== Public Role ==

Solaran became the language of daily civic life. It was used for contracts, markets, newspapers, military communication, street signs, parliamentary politics, and most state information intended for the general public.

Formal state ritual retained an Elder Tongue layer. Old source material says official edicts could be proclaimed first in Solra and then followed by a Solaran translation, allowing ceremonial continuity without excluding the wider population from understanding state orders.

Source material also links Solaran language culture to [[Sonism]], though the religion's doctrine and institutions still need a dedicated pass.

== Sunline Standard ==

The [[Solaran Alphabet]] was adopted in 1898 after a reform project commissioned by the [[Solaran Parliament]] in 1895. The change made Solaran easier to teach than the Elder Tongue abugida and compatible with modern printing, schoolbooks, newspapers, and bureaucratic forms.

The [[Solaran Language Office]] maintained spelling standards, public terminology, and official usage. Its work helped make Solaran a modern administrative and educational language without fully displacing the older ceremonial register.

Modern vernacular writing also supported [[Solaran Literature]]. [[Jane Pensworth]] began writing [[A Wild World]] in 1897, during the same reform era that made printed Solaran easier to teach and circulate.

== Dialects And Education ==

Source material describes coastal and mountain dialect variation but treats the dialects as mutually intelligible. This draft preserves dialect variation as a cultural fact without creating separate regional dialect pages until Solara's internal geography is reviewed.

In education, Solaran and Sunline were taught first. Elder Tongue instruction was reserved for advanced priestly, archival, legal, or administrative tracks, reinforcing the divide between mass literacy and elite ceremonial literacy.

== Canon Notes ==

The extracted source gives post-1994 speaker numbers and later language-office references. This 1994-back draft uses the language history and institutional structure but does not treat 2008-2010 demographic or curriculum references as 1994 canon.

The source's phonology and glyph tables contain corrupted characters from the dump. This draft keeps the high-level language relationship and institutional role rather than hardening a broken orthographic table.
